Later researchers considered H. exsul to be a synonym of Hemichromis letourneauxi. This point of view became doubted when Lothar Seegers in 1998 published a photo of a Hemichromis that he had collected in lake Turkana. That fish looked totally different from all Hemichromis letourneauxi known so far. Sadly almost never any freshwater fish from Kenya are exported, so H. exsul stayed a phantom.

Specimens of this species could be sourced for the first time this year. They were bred, and the first German bred Hemichromis exsul are now available from there.
Hemichromis exsul was described scientifically already in 1933 under the name Pelmatochromis exsul. The type locality was lake Rudolf (now: lake Turkana) in Kenya.

Red jewel cichlids are wonderful aquarium fishes despite the fact that sometimes very quarrelsome individuals appear. For scientists the complex of species of red jewel cichlids remains a mess. Many meristic features overlap and additionally many species are highly polychromatic.

Hemichromis exsul differs from all other Hemichromis known so far by the dark, blackish rims of the fins. Moreover the typical lateral blotch exhibited by most red jewel cichlids is missing in most animals. The fish stays rather small and is very peaceful – at least for a red jewel cichlid.
